en: The way the show works is...

A big record company promises a major debut to whoever can
win their way through the tournament.
Haruka-chan's right in the middle of competing in the finals.
She made it to the finals!? That's incredible! I mean, isn't it?
It is! It really is! She's a talented girl.
Park-san was absolutely set on having Haruka-chan win...
And then puttin' on a major concert in Tokyo for her debut.
But there's no guarantee she'll win!

Right. But that's how much Park-san was willin' to bet on
Haruka-chan and her abilities.

But I guess Haruka-chan really shouldn't be appearin' on the
show now that Park-san is gone.

She probably should hold off on that kind of thing for the
time being.
No way. She has to go on. No matter what.
Because that was Park-san's dream.

Haruka-chan, remember how I told you Park-san came to borrow
money from me?
Well, that 300 million yen she borrowed...
That was a fund to produce a concert in Tokyo.
Really!? You sure about that!?
Positive. Well, probably not the whole 300 million.

Some of that was likely for other promotional activities in
Tokyo, but that's beside the point.

She came to borrow money from me because she was that
confident Haruka-chan would win.

But, if I remember right, Park-san borrowed that money
from you⑬
A year and a half ago.
Then, that means⑬

Exactly. She made up her mind the instant she met
Haruka-chan.

She was going to see to it that Haruka-chan had that concert
in Tokyo, no matter what.
Of course, at the time, I had no idea the money was for you, Haruka-chan...
Park-san did all of that... for me?
That's why you can't just give up on her dream.

If you don't keep her dream alive, all her efforts will have
been in vain.
Haruka-chan, I know how you feel about Park-san.

So I won't try to stop you from looking into her death with
me.
But at the same time...

I'll do it. I'll do both. Carrying on her dream is every bit
as important to me as finding out the truth about her death.

And there you go. There's the girl Park-san and Kiryu-san
saw something special in.
And you, Horie-chan. We're counting on you.

It'll be your job to make sure our Haruka-chan here gets to
that Princess whatever-it-is.

Yes! I'll make sure! But, to be honest, I'm not sure how,
now that the money is gone...
That's why I'm getting that three hundred million back⑬to make her dream come true.
And in order to do that, we need to investigate her death.
Akiyama-san... All right, I'm in.
But how do we go about investigating her death?
I think the key lies in that suicide note.
Her note?
If it wasn't a suicide, it means the killer fabricated it.
Horie-chan, you said you thought it looked like her handwriting.
I saw it, too, but... Ah!

Come to think of it, Park-san hurt her hand a little while
ago. Her right hand.

But she said she used to write with her left hand, so she
just went back to doing that.
Okay, so she would've used her left hand to write that note.
Provided she was the one who wrote it, of course.

But if that note is written in the handwriting style of her
right hand...
Then somebody forged it.

And that would mean that her death was only made to look
like a suicide⑬by her killer.
I think it's time we took a look at that note for ourselves.

You said the police would give it back after the handwriting
was evaluated, right?
That's right. They didn't think it'd take too long.
Okay, we'll wait until then.
I probably should do at least a little work for my company...

And if there's anything you want to do, Haruka-chan, now
would be the time to do it.

No, that's all right. I'll just wait here. I can't do
anything else at a time like this.
Well, this might be your only chance.

You have the Princess League finals coming up, right? No way
you'll be able to do anything else once that rolls around.

So anything you need to do now, you'd better do while you
have time to spare.
When you put it that way... All right.

Good. If the police contact me, I'll let you know. You just
take it easy.
This is Akiyama-san from Sky Finance in Tokyo.
Horie-san asked him to come discuss Park-san.
He did, huh...? I see.
Akiyama-san, this is Yamaura-san.
She works at the agency. She's my vocal coach, too.

Howdy... Listen, Haruka. If ya want a voice lesson, you can
come to the studio.
Christina is here, too.

We gotta do something to distract ourselves at a time like
this, right?
I'll see ya later.
So this is where it happened, huh...?
(What else do I need to know?)
Haruka-chan, about what time did the incident happen?

This morning at about six. People in the neighborhood heard
the impact.
I wonder where she was supposed to have jumped from...
Akiyama-san... They say this is where she jumped.
Hmm. Seems like a good spot to fabricate a suicide, if you ask me.

What about that shoe thing people sometimes do when they
commit suicide? Were her shoes taken off and left neatly on the spot?
Yes, apparently so.
Hmm. Very textbook. A practically model suicide.
Somehow, that doesn't really seem like Park-san, either.
If you ask me, this whole thing reeks.
How far down is it from here?

Hmm. At this height, there's no guarantee. You'd have to try
and fall head first.

If you landed feet first, you might end up with some
compound fractures, but you'd definitely pull through.

And on a busy street like this, wouldn't you worry about
maybe hurting somebody else?
Wouldn't you pick a better spot if you were going to jump?
Yes, I think you might be right.

If it were me, I'd pick someplace higher, where I could be
sure I'd die instantly.
I guess that's about all we're gonna find out from this place.
You've seen enough, Akiyama-san?
Yeah. But I don't see any definite proof of a faked suicide.
Wanna head back down?
Now, let's see. Where to start?

If we want to prove that it was a murder, we'd better have a
look at the scene.
Although, that might be hard for you, Haruka-chan.
I'll be all right.

Okay. Good on you for keeping your chin up... Now, where do
they think she jumped from?
From the roof of this building. It's the fifth floor.
Okay, let's head on up and see what we can learn.
And they're certain it was a suicide?

There was a note. Sounds like the police will have it back
to us pretty soon. The handwriting's being evaluated.
As far as I could tell, though, it was her writing.
Given that, the police are pretty sure it's suicide.
I see... So she left a note, huh?

The detective said that, lately, suicides are on the rise
among executives of smaller companies. He sees it all the time, apparently.
Yeah, you do hear about that kind of thing a lot, I guess...
So what did her note say?
It was really short. Just two sentences.
All she wrote was, "I'm tired. I'm sorry."
"I'm tired. I'm sorry." That's it?
That doesn't sound like her.
I thought the same thing.
What do you think happened to her?
To be honest, I don't really know.

From a business standpoint, she had a lot of enemies, but,
as far as I know, none of that was enough to make her wanna kill herself.

But there's one more very serious problem I wanted to talk
to ya about...
It's about the money Park-san borrowed from you.

I looked in the safe earlier to check on it, and it wasn't
there anymore.
So you think it was stolen?
And the person who took it murdered Park-san?
Well, I can't say for sure, of course.

There's always the possibility Park-san moved it somewhere
recently.

If I could find the account book Park-san kept, I might be
able to tell you something, but it hasn't turned up yet.

Still, I wanted to let you know there's a chance the money's
been stolen.

If that's the case, quite honestly, I don't see how we
could ever pay you back.
Oh, of course not. I'd never ask you to pay.

I lent the money to Park-san personally, after all, not to
Dyna Chair.
Yes, I know, but still. It's such a large sum of money...

Anyway, now that all this has happened, what's the agency
going to do?

I don't know... Park-san always ran everything herself.
I really can't imagine what we'll do without her.

But there's this one new girl Park-san had been pouring all
her energy into. She's just about to make her big debut.
A new girl, huh?

Yeah, she has great promise. A real gem, this girl.
Park-san went all the way to Okinawa to find her.

Park-san put so much time and effort into nurturing her. If
the agency were to close now, all of that would go to waste.
I know Park-san would've hated that.

Horie-chan, it sounds to me like you don't think she
committed suicide.

You better believe I don't. The Park-san I knew never
would've done that.
I have to say, I agree with you.
What about you, Akiyama-san? What are your plans after this?

I plan to do some poking around on my own. I am a
moneylender, after all. Wouldn't be very good at my job
if I didn't keep track of my loans.
If somebody did kill her and took the money...
Then I'll just have to get it back.

And with what you told me, I doubt we can count on the
police helping out.

If I really want to find out the truth behind her death,
then I guess I'll just have to do it myself.
So who was the last person to see Park-san alive?

The new girl I told you about earlier. She's in the studio
on the fourth floor right now. I'll show you the way up.
Nah, that's all right. I'll figure it out.
Evenin'.
Oh, Saejima. Come on in.
Please, make yourself at home.
'Preciate it, Mama.
So they're coming for you tonight, huh?
Heh. Who would've thought you'd go from breaking out of one of the highest security prisons down in Okinawa to serving time all the way up in Abashiri? One end of Japan to the other.
Like some kinda magic trick.
Might not be so bad though. If you behave, you'll be out in what, two years?
So I hear.
In the meantime, we've got the Tojo Clan and the Omi Alliance still duking it out. As long as they're roughly equal in power, the yakuza world order is maintained.
But if anything ever tips the scales one way or the other, a war will be the least of our worries.
It'll leave an opening that foreign mafias will come in and exploit. Not to mention all the two-bit street gangs who don't have to worry about anti-yakuza laws.
That's why even us cops want to see the Tojo Clan back to its former heights. Ironic, huh?
I dunno, makes pretty good sense to me. Rather have the devil ya know than the one ya don't. 'Specially if that devil's already on a leash.
Too bad the Tojo Clan has far bigger problems than its lack of quality footsoldiers.
The leadership's been more or less gutted. All that's left now is plain old businessmen who only know how to do one thing: make money.
The numbers look good on the surface, sure. But those numbers are just papering over some serious cracks that'll find their way to the surface eventually.
Take that dustup with the Ueno Seiwa Clan. Low-tier would be a compliment for them, but they still managed to take the Tojo for a ride.
Not only that, but some of the more remote subsidiaries are turning their backs on the clan. The Tojo's not much more than a husk of its former self these days.
I know. That's why I'm goin' behind bars again.
A baptism by fire. One that'll see you end up captain of the Tojo Clan when you get out.
First n' foremost, I'm makin' amends. That has to come before anythin' else.
Smart. There're plenty of oldhand Tojo guys who are pissed about how you walked back into the clan.
But this'll prove your worth. Keep your own clan members from stabbing you in the back. Bet you long for the days when the cops were the only ones you had to watch out for.
Looks like our old friend's gone for good this time, too. Meaning it's on you and Majima to shoulder the clan. Be Daigo's pillars.
Still, two years away is a long time. Whatever you do in there, don't get slapped with any extra time. You're pushing your luck with the Tojo as is.
Yeah, goes without saying.
Anyway, think I overstayed my welcome. I'll let you lovebirds get some alone time.
Hey, c'mon! You know we're glad to have you around.
Hehehe. Yes, it was no trouble at all. You're always welcome here.
Yeah... Come back safe, Saejima.
Will do. See ya.
How to Play Count-Up
In this game, the numbers you hit are added to your score. When all rounds are concluded, the player with the higher score is declared the winner.
In Count-Up, both the outer and inner bull are worth 50 points.
